name: Jeshebeab
overview: Jeshebeab was a male Levite who served as the fourteenth chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron, which distinguished his priestly heritage within the tribe of Levi. His role is specifically noted in the division of priestly duties, highlighting his part in the organized worship of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshebeab means 'father lives,' a proper name recorded in Scripture without indication that it was divinely given. This meaning may reflect a testimony to God's ongoing life and faithfulness, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Jeshebeab is identified as a descendant of Ithamar, situating him within that particular priestly lineage. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him apart from his tribal and ancestral connections.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshebeab's significance lies in his appointment as the fourteenth priestly leader among the twenty-four courses established by King David to regulate temple worship. Being from the line of Ithamar, his inclusion underscores the continued priestly service of this branch of Aaron's descendants. His role reflects the orderly and divinely appointed structure for ministering before the Lord, which was vital for maintaining holiness and proper worship in Israel.
